/200-podcast-episodes-lessons/: Two hundred episodes in, I share what I know for sure about email, visibility and building a business that lasts. I talk about why you don't have to be loud, just consistent, why email is still my ride-or-die, and why visibility is about alignment, not algorithms. If you've ever wondered whether it's worth it or why it's taking so long, this one is for you.
/2023-black-friday-revealed/: I go behind the scenes of my 2023 Black Friday numbers, offer by offer, including the one that didn't sell at all because I hadn't primed my audience for it. I also share why that same offer sold three spots at $497 when I relaunched it later in 2024. Then we look at how to plan your own Black Friday, whether you want to sell, grow your list or nurture your audience.
/3-day-launch-strategy/: You don't need a new product to have a launch. I share the three-day launch I've been using to sell something I already have, what I send on each of the three days, and how to create urgency without automatically discounting. Heading into Black Friday 2026, it's a reminder that the season is a reason to sell what you've already made, not a reason to create something new.
/3-visibility-moves-scale-2026/: A lot of business owners are showing up and being visible, and growth still feels oddly stalled. I share three visibility moves for 2026: depth over distribution, rooms over audiences, and visibility with direction. The idea is to choose where you show up, build trust faster and give people a clear next step, so growth feels calmer and more sustainable.
/4-steps-to-plan-for-2026/: Planning a new year doesn't have to mean a colour-coded planner you abandon by February. I take you behind the scenes of the four steps I'm using to plan 2026: starting with life before business, reviewing the past year with honesty not judgment, building revenue around my actual capacity, and mapping the year with flexibility. The aim is a year that supports you instead of squeezing you.
/44-audit-more-than-5k-mastermind/: I launched a $44 Business Breakthrough Audit as a simple, low-pressure offer, and women started telling me it gave them more clarity than a $5,000 mastermind. I share how the audits work, why being met exactly where you are can beat more content, and what it taught me about going deeper instead of bigger. Plus a question to ask yourself about where you might be overcomplicating things.
/5-step-organization-system/: Struggling to find that one PDF again? I chat with professional organiser and life coach Tracey Hoth about her five steps to organise anything: sort, purge, assign homes, set limits and maintain. We cover her five master folders for your digital files, how the same system works in Canva, Gmail and your bookmarks bar, and how to use it on your calendar and to-do list.
/5-tips-for-email-subject-lines/: You can write the best email in the world, but it doesn't matter if no one opens it. I share five strategies for writing subject lines that get opened: using curiosity, creating genuine urgency, personalising, leading with a benefit and keeping it short. I also cover the common mistakes to avoid and why testing and tweaking your subject lines pays off.
/alison-hardy-email-list-growth/: I chat with Allison Hardy about how she grew her email list from 4,000 to over 10,000 subscribers without ads or social media. She used a bundle strategy, ran eight bundles in 2024 and repurposed existing freebies instead of creating new ones. Allison shares what she learned about choosing the right bundles, nurturing new subscribers, and why she'd tell you to start small.
/angela-henderson-event-strategy/: What if your next growth moment had nothing to do with funnels and everything to do with genuine connection? I chat with Angela Henderson about her live event of 100 attendees where nobody sold from stage, and how it led to over $300K in mastermind sales through follow-up. We also cover her four types of buyers and the inner work that sits behind visibility.
/apple-mail-ai-summaries/: Apple Mail is rolling out AI-generated summaries that replace the preview text you've been optimising, so what does that mean for your open rates? I explain what's changing in plain English, why your sender name, subject line and first few sentences matter more now, and five steps to adapt so your emails still get opened. No panic required.
/australian-women-in-business-conference: Real growth isn't always about the next big strategy. I share three unexpected takeaways from the Australian Women in Business Conference 2024, hosted by Angela Henderson Consulting: the power of being in a room with like-minded women, how a silent disco and a hug meditation shifted something strategy couldn't, and why it pays to embrace the unexpected.
/be-seen-by-the-right-people-visibility-: Being visible doesn't mean being profitable. I explain the biggest visibility mistake I see, trying to be everywhere for everyone, and the three things that turn visibility into clients: getting in the right rooms, nailing your message and always giving a next step. I also share three questions to audit your visibility and why positioning is usually the real issue.
/become-your-own-publicist-gloria-chou/: Think PR is only for celebrities and influencers? I chat with PR coach Gloria Chou about how to become your own publicist in as little as 15 minutes a day. She walks through her CPR pitching method (credibility, point of view and relevance), how to find the right journalists, and why a small audience won't hold you back from getting featured.
/best-email-templates-or-funnels/: I'm not anti-template, but I am against copy-and-paste marketing that makes you sound like everyone else. I talk about why swipe files and cookie-cutter funnels fall flat, why we're in a trust recession, and how to customise templates so they sound like you. If your funnel isn't converting, it might be a voice problem rather than a tech problem.
/best-performing-emails-april/: I pull back the curtain on my April email numbers: how many emails I sent, my best performing email at a 51.2% open rate and 1.8% click rate, and the affiliate email that came in second. I also share how I added 346 new subscribers with one bundle, one summit and one workshop, and the two problems to look for in your own list: nurture and visibility.
/best-practices-for-your-email-list/: What should you actually send your email list, and how often? I share the types of emails that engage subscribers, from welcome and educational emails to behind-the-scenes, launch and roundup emails, and why I recommend a consistent weekly send. I also cover selling versus nurturing, keeping templates in your own voice, what to expect with unsubscribes and action steps for today.
/big-deal-energy-leanne-sia/: When was the last time you walked into a room and truly owned your presence? I chat with Leanne Sia, creator of the Big Deal Energy framework, about what it is and how to access it every day. We cover setting boundaries without guilt, overcoming fear of rejection, using a power song to boost confidence, and the role authenticity plays in lasting success.
/black-friday-wont-save-your-business/: Black Friday won't fix low sales, messy positioning or a cold email list. It simply amplifies whatever foundation you already have, good or bad. I explain why discounting isn't the shortcut it looks like, how to tell whether you have a volume or a messaging problem, and the three ways to approach Black Friday: lead, nurture or sell.
/build-email-list-without-social-media-a: Imagine it's day one with no list, no audience and no ad budget. I share what I'd ignore completely (daily Instagram posting, generic freebies and ads before anything is validated), then the steps I'd take instead: one strong lead magnet, two or three aligned visibility plays like bundles, podcasts and freebie swaps, a consistent weekly email, and relationships built with care.
/burned-by-a-mastermind-before/: Most women in business don't need another strategy. They need to loosen their grip. I share a personal story I've never brought to the podcast before, about being burned by a mastermind, and what that does to your nervous system. We look at the difference between effort and expansion, and why growth responds to clarity rather than pressure.
/claude-claude-code-chrome-extension-del: I thought I was already pretty good at using AI, until my biz bestie Anita Mac showed me what Claude could really do. We cover the difference between Claude.ai, Claude Code and the Chrome extension, her human-AI sandwich for keeping your voice in your content, why Projects are worth using, and the small habits that stop your tokens running out. You'll also hear how she built a full sales page in under two hours.
/clean-email-list-reengage-subscribers/: Growing your list matters, but a big list won't help if nobody is opening your emails. I walk you through cleaning it in three steps: segment your inactive subscribers, run a three-part re-engagement sequence before you delete anyone, then let go of those who don't respond. The payoff is better open rates, deliverability and sales.
/collaboration-partner-invited-back/: After more than 130 collaborations, I've noticed the people who get invited back aren't always the ones with the biggest email lists. This solo episode shares five ways to become someone people love to work with: make your pitch easy to say yes to, follow through, care about the host's success, stay in touch afterwards, and bring ideas.
/consistent-course-sales-caitlin-bacher/: If you're stuck on the launch hamster wheel of plan, hype, launch, crash and repeat, there's another way. I chat with Caitlin Bacher, founder of Scale With Success, about selling courses consistently with evergreen funnels, how she reached $1M in 9 months without launching, and the mistakes to avoid when going evergreen.
/customer-experience-strategy/: Your happiest customers are your strongest growth strategy. I chat with Madelyn Furlong about her three-part framework for turning clients into loyal, vocal fans: organisation, personalisation and going the extra mile. We also cover why storytelling sticks, the biggest mistake that blocks referrals, and simple steps to start without a big team or endless hours.
/customer-survey-questions/: Many of us write sales pages and plan offers based on assumptions about our audience. I chat with Nadine Nethery, an audience-driven copywriter turned customer experience strategist, about using simple, open-ended surveys instead. She shares her 10-question survey, how to sort the answers into objections, beliefs, desires and pain points, and how to research even without a big list.
/deeper-email-list-not-bigger/: You don't need a bigger list, you need a deeper one. After hosting a networking mixer just for my email list, I share why reach without relationships means nothing and what a deeper list actually looks like. You'll learn the three foundations of building one (personalisation, consistency and reciprocity) and what changes when you choose depth over width.
/doubled-email-list-without-social-media: In February 2024 my email list sat at 2,862 subscribers. By February 2025 it was 6,108, and I got there without social media. I share the V² Visibility Framework behind that growth, the bundles, summits, podcast guesting and freebie swaps that brought subscribers in (with the real numbers), and the biggest email mistakes I see, including not tracking what's working.
/drive-traffic-to-your-offer-mara-riopel: Mara Riopel and I have never had a catch-up where one of us wasn't walking through something hard, so this conversation, recorded for both of our podcasts, goes straight to the real stuff. We talk about building through heavy seasons, pivoting your business model when your capacity changes, the difference between visibility and traffic, and Mara's $23,000 mastermind lesson. You'll also hear why staying the course is the strategy most people skip.
/eft-tapping-for-entrepreneurs-jacqui-ac: Feeling stuck, burnt out or like you're falling short of your goals? I chat with Jacqui Acree, a certified EFT practitioner and mindset coach, about how EFT tapping works on your nervous system. We talk about reframing unmet goals and deadlines with self-compassion, why self-sabotage is often a form of protection, and how to rebuild self-trust.
/email-analytics-101/: Email analytics can feel overwhelming, but they're how you stop sending emails into a digital black hole. I walk through the four key metrics to track (open rate, click-through rate, unsubscribe rate and bounce rate), the industry benchmarks to compare yourself against, and simple tweaks to improve each one, so you can use the data to grow, nurture and sell.
/email-list-not-converting-positioning/: A client's summit speaker has a huge email list, yet got no clicks, no purchases and no engagement. I explain why volume doesn't drive conversion, clarity does, and what positioning actually is. You'll hear where lists go wrong at the growth stage, four questions to audit your message, and five ways to fix unclear positioning.
/email-list-quiet-january-what-to-do/: If your email list feels quiet right now, pause before you rewrite your funnel or change platforms. I explain why January inbox behaviour is different rather than worse, why email responds to trust and rhythm instead of pressure, and what not to change. You'll also get a simple place to start: one email that reintroduces you.
/email-marketing-2025/: Social media is getting louder and algorithms are getting tougher, but email is still your secret weapon. In this solo episode I explain why email should be your top focus in 2025: direct access to your audience, a list you own and strong ROI. We also cover personalised messaging, using your data, and speaking to different types of buyers.
/email-subscribers-vs-social-media-follo: Email subscribers reply more, click more, buy more and actually stick around. If you've been pouring hours into social media and watching people disappear, this one's for you. I explain why a subscriber is a conscious yes, why email is personal and algorithm-free, and four ways to keep subscribers for the long haul: value, personalisation, consistency and conversation.
/email-templates-liz-wilcox/: Email templates can make you sound like a robot, but they don't have to. I chat with Liz Wilcox about how to retype and read templates out loud so they sound like you, her Email Staircase method for turning followers into friends and friends into customers, her 20-minute newsletter formula, and why your from line matters more than your subject line.
/email-tips-to-improve-your-email-delive: If your emails don't reach the inbox, nothing else in your email marketing matters. I walk through the more technical side of deliverability, including authenticating your domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, why I delete cold subscribers regularly, how personalisation goes beyond a first name, and the spam triggers to avoid. You'll finish with clear action steps.
/emails-not-making-sales/: If your emails aren't making sales, you're not alone, because email marketing has changed. I share three simple shifts that help your emails connect and convert without feeling sleazy or spammy: moving from generic messages to segmented ones, from product-focused to relationship-centred content, and from single sales emails to a simple mini sales sequence.
/grow-business-without-social-media-post: More posting equals more visibility equals more sales is a lie, and I'm naming it. I explain why social media feels so heavy in 2025, why attention isn't the same as trust, and the three things that grow a business instead: clarity, connection and credibility. You'll also get four simple swaps to replace daily posting with visibility that compounds over time.
/grow-your-email-list-with-seo/: If Instagram disappeared tomorrow, would your business still grow? I talk with Laura Jawad about why SEO is pull marketing, how to check which keywords are already driving traffic to your website, and why most websites attract the wrong visitors. You'll also hear how to turn that traffic into email subscribers by giving people more than one chance to join your list.
/grow-your-email-list-without-social-med: I used this episode to introduce a membership I ran for women who felt stuck, frustrated and overwhelmed by growing their email list. I cover the relationship-based strategies it focused on (collaborations, bundles, guest speaking and freebie swaps), the trainings and tools that were inside, and the story of a member who finally felt in control of her list.
/growing-your-list-by-hosting-bundles/: Hosting free digital bundles is my favourite way to grow my email list in 2024. I explain what a bundle is and how it works, why it brings exposure, higher quality subscribers, new relationships and room to scale, and what's involved in hosting one, from choosing a specific theme and recruiting contributors to setting up a landing page. I'm honest about the work involved too.
/high-converting-sales-email-formulas/: Writing sales emails can feel awkward, and it's easy to overthink every one. I break down five formulas that work without being pushy: Problem-Solution, Storytelling, Objection-Handling, Social Proof and Scarcity-Urgency (used responsibly). You'll hear how each one works, when to use it, and why picking just one to test and refine is enough.
/high-ticket-and-low-ticket-business-mod: The idea that you have to pick between a high-ticket or low-ticket business model is outdated, so toss it. I explain why a layered offer suite works better, how high-ticket, low-ticket and free content each do a different job, and how many of my highest-level clients started with free content and moved up. A clear next step makes upgrades feel natural.
/how-can-i-make-money-inside-my-business: This is a replay of a 1:1 strategy call with one of my members, built around the question of how to make money in your business quickly. We talk through adding live calls and organising membership tiers, why knowing her niche matters for lead generation, how to use an email list to bring in recurring revenue from a mini membership, and how your emotional state shapes your business communication.
/how-people-are-buying-2025/: 'Charge what you're worth' falls flat in 2025, because buyers don't care what you're worth if they don't trust you'll deliver. I explain the trust recession, why that advice skips strategy, and the three things buyers want before they say yes: clarity, connection and confidence in you. A client story shows how reworked messaging, not a lower price, got her sales moving.
/how-to-create-a-freebie-that-actually-c: Ever created a freebie that got crickets? I chat with Jillian Leslie about why most freebies don't convert, the six psychological purchasing triggers your offers can tap into, and why a simple cheat sheet or checklist beats a polished ebook. You'll also hear what to do if your current freebie isn't working and how to reverse engineer a lead magnet from your main offer.
/how-to-level-up-your-email-marketing-fo: Once your list passes 1000, your email strategy needs to level up too. I cover why segmentation matters (and how to start simply with clients and non-clients), how a product ladder gives subscribers ways to buy at different price points, and how to pre-sell an idea before you create it. The biggest takeaway is to focus on just one of these at a time.
/how-to-nurture-your-email-list-with-sop: I chat with marketing coach Sophia Parra about how to nurture your email list and start real conversations. We talk through her three pillars (growing your audience, nurturing your audience and making sales), why engagement matters more than social media numbers, and nurturing ideas like exclusive events for subscribers and personalised videos, so selling feels like a natural next step.
/how-to-sell-to-your-email-list/: Lots of us feel uncomfortable selling, so I talk about how to sell to your email list and when to start. I share why thinking of selling as serving helps, why selling is a skill you build with practice (a bit like learning to ride a bike), and why the answer to when is from the start. I also cover accepting unsubscribes and tracking your open and click rates.
/how-to-write-authentic-email-copy-that-: I sit down with Marisa Corcoran, copy expert and creator of The Copy Confidence Society, to talk about writing email copy that sounds like you. She explains why copy matters across your whole business, her word closet and accessories closet for bringing your personality into your writing, why being specific beats being a generalist, and how copy builds relationships, not just sales.
/if-i-was-growing-my-email-list-from-zer: Starting an email list from zero can feel overwhelming, so I share my own list growth journey and what I'd do if I were starting again today. I explain why you only need one freebie, how to work backwards from your main offer to create it, where to promote it, and the collaboration strategies I'd use, like joining a bundle with no list size requirement.
/inside-the-inbox-season-2-may-2025/: I was fed up with cookie-cutter summits, so I created Inside The Inbox, an audio-only private podcast event. I explain why I made it, what's new in Season 2 (30+ speakers, episodes under 15 minutes, a quiz and one action step at the end of every episode), how it covers growing, nurturing and selling by email, and how a portion of profits from every VIP pass goes to Small Steps 4 Hannah.
/january-launch-strategy/: January launches start in December. This episode walks you through five simple steps to take now so you're not scrambling after the holidays: warm up your audience without being salesy, refine your messaging, build a pre-launch waitlist, organise a timeline and checklist, and tap into the January mindset. You'll head into the new year feeling ready, not rushed.
/julie-empress-case-study/: Julie C. Butler is a virtual summit coach who had the offers, funnels and systems and still felt like she was on a hamster wheel. I chat with Julie about why strategy matters more than more information, what changed when she stopped doing it alone, and how she tripled her income in 60 days. If you've done everything right and still feel stuck, this one is for you.
/low-lift-email-list-growth/: Back in 2022 I ran tiny audio pop-up events that grew my list by 100 to 150 people at a time, so in 2026 I brought them back. I share the real numbers from the first one (303 signups, 370+ downloads and one $97 season pass sale), what a free event is actually for, and how I find new collaborators without cold-pitching. It's about building a growth engine, not chasing one big win.
/loyal-to-your-coach-or-future-self/: Before strategy, funnels or visibility, I want to talk about loyalty, the quiet kind that keeps women in rooms they've already outgrown. I cover where loyalty turns into self-abandonment, how the sunken cost fallacy keeps you stuck, the signs it's time to move on, and why your loyalty belongs to your future self. If you've ever thought 'I know this isn't working anymore, but I already committed', this is for you.
/make-extra-1000-without-creating-new-of: When we want to make more money, our first instinct is to create another offer. I share the five places I look for an extra $1,000 before building anything new: what you already sell, unused capacity, forgotten content, your audience and your skills. I also cover working the maths backwards, what I wouldn't do for quick cash, and the experiment I'm running with my own podcast.
/mistakes-to-avoid-when-using-collaborat: Collaborations can grow your email list fast, but only if you go about them the right way. I share the mistakes I've made so you don't have to (being passive, skipping the relationship and making it one-sided), then how to find aligned partners and pitch them so it's a win for both of you. You'll leave with a clear, proactive approach instead of waiting for the perfect person to show up.
/monetise-email-list-no-launch/: If the only time your email list makes you money is when you launch your own offer, you're leaving cash on the table. I share three ways to monetise your list that aren't selling your own offers: sponsorships (with pricing ranges), affiliate offers and collaborative paid bundles. I also explain my 80/20 rule for earning from your list without losing your audience's trust.
/more-ways-to-be-discovered/: What if your audience isn't too small, and the real issue is that not enough people can find you? I explain why 'no one wants this' is often a discovery problem, the difference between audience size and audience security, and my doors framework for not relying on one platform. You'll also get a simple action step to audit your doors and build just one more.
/my-skool-experiment/: I started a Skool community expecting it to be fine, and within days over 130 people from my email list had joined and the conversations got real. I share my honest thoughts on why small rooms build deeper trust, why accessibility beats attendance, why this isn't an 'email is dead' conversation, and what I'm learning about voice of customer, fun and depth.
/my-v2-visibility-framework-how-you-can-: Social media is unpredictable, but your email list is something you own. I walk you through my V2 Visibility Framework, with collaboration-based strategies on one side (summits, bundles, freebie swaps and podcast guesting) and search and SEO-driven strategies on the other. I also cover how to choose which one to try and how to know if it's working.
/my-word-of-the-year-2025/: Since 2020 I've chosen one word each year to guide my decisions, and this episode shares how I do it. I look back at the words that shaped the past five years (Breathe, Adapt, Play, Build and Balance), explain why I chose Bold for 2025, and give you tips for choosing your own word so it becomes an anchor for your year.
/nurture-new-subscribers-post-event/: Growing your list is the exciting part, but then comes the question of what to send once those new subscribers arrive. I share the biggest mistake people make after a summit, bundle or podcast feature, and exactly how I nurtured 700+ new subscribers after Inside The Inbox Season 2, from one 'Start Here' email to simply inviting them to hit reply. List growth isn't the problem, it's what you do next.
/nurture-your-email-list-evergreen-email: Your email list isn't cold, it's under-nurtured. I sit down with Cheryl Rerick to talk about what happens after someone joins your list, what evergreen email sequences are (and aren't), why customer research matters more than your tech, and how to audit your offers before you automate anything. We also get into repeating your core message without boring yourself to death.
/one-story-that-sells-kris-jones/: If your content feels chaotic or you're constantly second-guessing what to say, one story might be the fix. I chat with messaging strategist Kris Jones about her One Story method, what makes a brand story work, where to use it across your marketing, and a quick story audit you can do right now. It's about selling more by saying less.
/pausing-isnt-quitting-strategic-busines: There's a season no one warns you about, where you're not failing but things aren't really working either. I share the client call that led to a Pause Plan, what a strategic pause actually looks like, and a gentle plan you can steal. Pausing isn't quitting, and it might be the most strategic move you make.
/pinterest-seo-strategy-heather-farris/: Pinterest isn't social media, it's a visual search engine, which makes it a long game that works in the background. I chat with Pinterest strategist Heather Farris about how to build a Pinterest SEO plan, what the traffic looks like with real client numbers, how to save time with AI and PinBot, and what to do if your account is a mess.
/plan-for-2025/: The new year sneaks up fast, so I share the four steps I'm taking in November 2024 to plan for 2025. I cover the common planning mistakes, then my process: planning life first, looking back before moving forward, mapping out revenue goals and syncing it all with your calendar. The aim is a year that fits your real life, not just your business.
/plan-rest-of-year-without-burning-out/: Halfway through the year, I always ask myself whether I'm doing all of this because it works or because I'm supposed to. I chat with Katherine Mackenzie-Smith, creator of the Cozy Business framework, about why copying someone else's system rarely lasts, how to review the first half of your year, and why a 90-day plan beats a 12-month one. We also cover checking in with your capacity each day and knowing what actually moves the needle.
/podcast-rebrand-welcome-to-the-email-gr: Time for a proper reintroduction. After a lot of reflection and planning, I rebranded the podcast as The Email Growth Show to better serve female entrepreneurs who want to grow their email lists without the stress of social media or paid ads. I share how I went from wedding photographer to email marketing strategist, and what to expect from here: weekly episodes, monthly guest interviews and practical tips you can act on straight away.
/podcast/episodes/100-members-signed-up-: I pull back the curtain on how over 100 women joined The Spotlight Club, my new membership, within three months of launching. I share how I came up with the idea, why high ticket offers felt so gross to me at the time and why I chose something more accessible at $19 a month, and how I overdeliver inside the membership, which is the key to it all.
/podcast/episodes/2022-debrief-and-takea: This is the last episode of 2022, and I debrief the year. I share what worked well, what didn't work at all and everything in between, as a behind-the-scenes look at year one of growing an online business, covering the wins, the challenges and the revenue.
/podcast/episodes/250-episodes-later-wha: Two hundred and fifty episodes in, I'm looking back at what multiple business pivots, burnout seasons and visibility experiments have taught me about building a business that lasts. This is a more personal episode, less how-to and more what I know to be true now: why consistency pays off, why relationships have created more opportunities than reach, and why building things you actually own matters.
/podcast/episodes/3-benefits-of-taking-f: Taking fast action can be the difference between seeing success in your business and not. In this solo episode I share why I believe in letting go of perfection and moving faster, and the three benefits you'll notice: fast tracking your progress, building momentum for yourself and your audience, and improving your own problem solving skills.
/podcast/episodes/3-common-misconception: Virtual summits are far more accessible than most people think, whatever the size of your business. In this solo episode I debunk three common misconceptions: that they're complicated to put together, that you need a big audience to host one successfully, and that they cost a lot of money.
/podcast/episodes/3-questions-to-help-yo: If you're heading into maternity leave, it helps to plan before the baby arrives. In this solo episode I share three questions to ask yourself to baby proof your business: what your perfect maternity leave looks like, what you need to keep earning each month and what support you have in place, and which business must haves you can batch ahead, automate or outsource.
/podcast/episodes/3-reasons-you-need-to-: I believe community can change your life, and in this solo episode I share three reasons you need one around you as a mama and entrepreneur. Being a mum and a business owner is hard and not everyone can relate, community can stop you feeling overwhelmed or burnt out, and community plus collaboration is where the magic happens.
/podcast/episodes/3-strategies-to-get-wo: Working from home while raising babies is messy, and I chat with my friend Chelsea Wessman, a Productivity Consultant and Time Management Strategist, about making it sustainable. She shares three strategies: taking control of your time, setting boundaries for yourself and your kids, and training your brain to focus. We also cover becoming results oriented instead of task oriented, and what to do when your day still goes sideways.
/podcast/episodes/3-strategies-to-grow-y: I chat with Holly Haynes, who has grown her own full time business on a part time schedule. She shares how to put together a side hustle strategy and plan that works for you, so you can keep working towards your goals while still focusing on your priorities and your family.
/podcast/episodes/3-things-i-do-to-cope-: As a business owner and a mother, I know firsthand how anxiety can show up in both roles. In this solo episode I share three things I do to cope: making self-care non-negotiable through small daily habits, reducing over-stimulation (parenting earplugs included), and embracing uncertainty by letting go of control. I also cover keeping segmenting simple and finding a balance between email and the social platforms you enjoy.
/why-i-dont-send-welcome-sequences-anymo: I explain why welcome sequences started to feel off for my audience, what is changing in the inbox heading into 2026, and why the delivery email is usually the most-opened email you will ever send. Then I walk through what goes into a Start Here email (a human introduction, clear expectations, a few places to explore and an invitation to reply) so new subscribers feel welcomed instead of marched through a funnel.
/why-im-not-just-in-email-marketing-anym: Yes, I love and teach email marketing, but I'm not just in email marketing anymore. I also talk about what this means for the show, and for you if you're outgrowing your own box.
/why-you-should-overdeliver-in-your-free: Overdelivering builds trust and loyalty, and it's more cost-effective to keep clients than to constantly find new ones. I share practical ways to overdeliver in your free offers (quality over quantity) and your paid products (surprise bonuses, extra support), plus why boundaries matter so you don't burn out. You'll finish with small changes to try on your existing offers today.

I also share why sometimes the smartest move is to nurture the people already in your world.
/workshops-underrated-conversion-event/: People say you need funnels, ads and a massive audience to sell online, but the biggest growth spurts I see come from workshops. I explain why workshops convert when other things don't, the mistake of treating them like content, and a simple follow-up email structure to sell afterwards without feeling pushy. You don't need a bigger audience, just a clear topic and an hour.
